courses.title: Shema across the canon
courses.description: Six sessions from Torah declaration to Gemara reasoning.

sessions.title: Hear the address
sessions.hebrew: שמע ישראל ה׳ אלהינו ה׳ אחד
sessions.translation: Hear, Israel: the Lord is our God, the Lord is one.
sessions.explanation: Start with the source's own voice before its later uses.

sessions.title: Read the scope
sessions.hebrew: ואהבת את ה׳ אלהיך בכל לבבך ובכל נפשך ובכל מאדך
sessions.translation: Love the Lord your God with all your heart, being, and might.
sessions.prompt: What does the repeated ‘with all’ language do?
choices: It expands the scope of the command.
sessions.explanation: Repetition and expansion are literary evidence.

sessions.title: Carry words into life
sessions.hebrew: והיו הדברים האלה על לבבך ושננתם לבניך ודברת בם
sessions.translation: These words shall be upon your heart; teach them diligently and speak of them.
sessions.prompt: What movement does the passage make?
choices: From inward attention to teaching and speech.
From a final ruling to an objection.
sessions.explanation: The source connects heart, teaching, and recurring speech.

sessions.title: Meet the Siddur
sessions.hebrew: שמע ישראל ה׳ אלהינו ה׳ אחד
sessions.translation: The Torah line becomes recurring communal recitation.
sessions.prompt: What does the liturgical setting add?
sessions.explanation: Later use adds a role without erasing the original source.

sessions.title: Ask the Mishnah's question
sessions.translation: From when do we recite Shema in the evening?
sessions.prompt: What kind of question is this?
sessions.explanation: The Mishnah receives a known practice through a precise case.

sessions.title: Explain the Gemara's pressure
sessions.translation: On what is the tanna standing, that he teaches ‘from when?’
sessions.explanation: The learner can now follow a Torah line through prayer, practice, and argument.

production.prompt: You met these two words in Session 1 and again in the Siddur. Type their English meaning from memory.

courses.title: Blessings as a source chain
courses.description: Six sessions from receiving a gift to studying its legal reception.

sessions.title: Read the sequence
sessions.translation: You shall eat, be satisfied, and bless.
sessions.explanation: The verse supplies an ordered source for later study.

sessions.title: Name the object of gratitude
sessions.hebrew: על הארץ הטבה אשר נתן לך
sessions.translation: For the good land that He has given you.
sessions.prompt: What does the verse join to blessing?
choices: A received gift and its source.
sessions.explanation: The verse frames blessing as response to received goodness.

sessions.title: See a communal form
sessions.translation: Three who ate together join in an invitation to bless.
sessions.explanation: A later source can specify how a theme enters shared practice.

sessions.title: Ask what Gemara adds
sessions.hebrew: כל הנהנה מן העולם הזה בלא ברכה
sessions.translation: Whoever benefits from this world without a blessing…
sessions.prompt: What should a reader ask next?
choices: What claim or pressure this adds to the practice.
Which word is easiest to memorize.
sessions.explanation: Gemara reading asks what work a statement performs.

sessions.title: Keep the boundary
choices: The difference between study and personal ruling.
sessions.explanation: Seder teaches source literacy, not personal psak.

sessions.title: State the chain
sessions.prompt: Which account best maps the unit?
choices: A Torah response becomes communal practice and later reasoning.
Each source erases the earlier one.
sessions.explanation: You can now trace a source across genres while preserving their differences.

production.translation: You shall eat, be satisfied, and bless.
production.prompt: This phrase opened the course. Type its English meaning from memory, in a few words.
acceptable: you shall eat be satisfied and bless
you will eat be satisfied and bless
you shall eat and be satisfied and bless
and you shall eat and be satisfied and bless
